conduit#229 talent-community consent RPCs. r7_issue_talent_pool_consent_token mints a single-use token (re-checks caller tenant membership when auth.uid() is non-null); r7_redeem_talent_pool_consent validates a SHA-256-hashed single-use 30-day token and sets consent. SECURITY DEFINER is required to write across tenant RLS with token-gated authz inside the function. Intentional, live-verified on prod 2026-06-24.

conduit#229 public talent-community opt-in. r7_redeem_talent_pool_consent is the ONLY anon-reachable write in conduit by design: it is token-gated (32-byte raw token, SHA-256 hash compare), single-use, 30-day expiry, non-enumerating, returns no PII. Equivalent to a magic-link. Live-verified on prod 2026-06-24 (consent flip + token consumed).

crm7#1123 tenant-switch authority. set_current_tenant(p_tenant_id) is membership-gated — it raises 'Unauthorized: not an active member of the target tenant' unless the caller has an active public.user_tenants row for p_tenant_id, then persists profiles.current_tenant_id. log_tenant_switch(...) is its audit-write companion (the tenant_switch_audit direct-INSERT forgery fix routes all audit writes through this SECDEF fn rather than allowing direct client INSERT). Both MUST be EXECUTE-grantable to authenticated (they are the client RPCs for switching tenant context); both are SECURITY DEFINER (write profiles / read user_tenants / write audit under RLS) with search_path pinned to 'public, pg_temp'. Live-verified body 2026-07-20 via pg_get_functiondef. Accepted-by-design; not a category waiver.

Developer-portal Feature Builder apply path (north-star chain, 2026-07-22). Executes author-supplied migration SQL, so it is arbitrary-DDL by design and MUST be SECURITY DEFINER. Mitigations: (1) hard internal gate — raises 42501 unless caller's profiles.platform_role IN ('developer','platform_admin'); (2) full audit trail to feature_migration_log (actor, SQL, status, error); (3) search_path pinned to public,pg_temp; (4) EXECUTE revoked from public/anon — authenticated-only, same class as delete_organization / set_current_tenant precedents. Browser calls via supabase.rpc are required until a service-role edge-function proxy exists (tracked: developer-portal hardening backlog).

rules.reason: TGA training-provider / qualifications-catalog RPCs (crm7 20260802184000, 20260805210000). Both are called from the browser by an ordinary tenant user and BOTH re-enforce authorisation inside the function rather than relying on the grant. import_qualification_from_catalog(p_tenant_id, p_catalog_code): needs SECURITY DEFINER only to read catalog.qualifications, a schema authenticated cannot select. It raises 42501 unless the caller is a member of p_tenant_id (auth_tenant_id()), and for the CREATE branch additionally requires owner/admin/manager (auth_tenant_id_with_role) — re-implementing tenant_insert_qualifications' WITH CHECK verbatim, so a bare member cannot insert a row their own table policy would reject. Reuse is checked first, so a member who may only read still gets an existing row. link_training_provider_to_organisation(p_training_provider_id, p_tenant_id): needs SECURITY DEFINER to write across the clients boundary; raises 42501 unless the caller is a member of p_tenant_id. NOTE, stated plainly rather than buried: this one is membership-gated ONLY — any tenant member may link a provider within their own tenant, with no owner/admin/manager requirement. That is deliberate per the function's own COMMENT, and the blast radius is confined to the caller's own tenant, but it is a weaker gate than its sibling and should be revisited if provider linkage ever becomes billable or externally visible. Both REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC and anon, GRANT only to authenticated, and pin search_path = public, pg_temp. Not a category waiver — reviewed function-by-function 2026-08-05 during the development->main promotion these two first reached.
rules.review: Revisit link_training_provider_to_organisation's membership-only gate if provider linkage becomes billable or cross-tenant visible.

rules.reason: Pay-run builder (crm7 20260806043000/053000/060000). Called from the browser by a payroll operator, so an EXECUTE grant to authenticated is the point of it, not an oversight. SECURITY DEFINER is required to write pay_runs and payroll_records atomically across their RLS policies. Authorisation does NOT rest on the grant: the function raises 42501 unless the caller holds owner/admin/manager on p_tenant_id via auth_tenant_id_with_role — a stricter tier than membership, because creating a pay run is a money event. REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC, anon; search_path pinned public, pg_temp. It also cannot silently over-pay: it excludes any timesheet already carried by an existing payroll_records row, so a re-run produces an empty run rather than paying twice, and it REFUSES (with a per-person reason) rather than pricing untiered overtime or an ambiguous rate. Every write it makes lands in a DRAFT run with paye_tax and net_pay at 0. Not a category waiver — reviewed against the function body 2026-08-06.
objects: build_pay_run_from_timesheets(p_tenant_id uuid, p_period_start date, p_period_end date, p_payment_date date)

rules.reason: Financial-reports summary card (crm7 20260806050000, corrected 20260806065000). READ-ONLY and takes no parameters — it aggregates the CALLER'S OWN invoices and returns four scalars (invoiced, paid, outstanding, overdue count). SECURITY DEFINER is used so the aggregate is computed server-side in one pass rather than shipping every invoice row to the browser to be summed. Tenant scoping is enforced INSIDE the function — `where i.tenant_id in (select auth_tenant_id())` — so a caller can only ever aggregate tenants they belong to, and there is no argument through which another tenant could be named. REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC, anon; search_path pinned public, pg_temp. It writes nothing. Not a category waiver — reviewed against the function body 2026-08-06.
